title: Coroutine Concurrency and Shared Mutable State
platform_conditions: Kotlin/JVM with kotlinx.coroutines; applies on both server JVM and Android runtime (Dispatchers.Default/IO share worker threads on both)
security_mechanism: Coroutines do not serialize memory: a suspend call can resume on a different worker thread, so a plain var or shared collection touched across a suspension point is a data race, not just a logic bug. GlobalScope.launch escapes structured concurrency — the work outlives its scope, cannot be cancelled with the caller, and its failures surface as an unhandled exception in a process-wide handler (on Android this crashes the app; on a server it can bypass the request's error path). launch/async swallow the body's exception until join/await is called, so a failed authorization write can disappear silently when the returned Deferred is never awaited.

source_sink_clues.source: Concurrent requests or UI events driving the same shared state; attacker-shaped inputs that race two interleaved coroutine runs against one check-then-act sequence.
source_sink_clues.sink: GlobalScope.launch / GlobalScope.async; reads and writes of shared vars or collections inside coroutines without Mutex/actor/confined dispatcher; check-then-act sequences separated by a suspension point (withContext, delay, network calls)

tracking_guards: Check shared state is confined: Mutex.withLock, atomic types, an actor/Channel serialized to one coroutine, or a single-threaded dispatcher owning the state; check coroutines run inside lifecycle- or request-scoped CoroutineScope instead of GlobalScope; check every async() result is awaited or its exception explicitly handled (supervisorScope + handler).
not_candidate_when: The state is immutable or constructed per-coroutine, the shared value is a confined single-threaded dispatcher's data, or the launch is an isolated fire-and-forget task with no shared memory and a handled failure path.
synthetic_safe_example: val mutex = Mutex(); launch { mutex.withLock { counter++ } }
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
